newsitem.title: USA: U.S. mortgage-backeds dive, yield spreads tighten.
newsitem.headline: U.S. mortgage-backeds dive, yield spreads tighten.

text.p: U.S. mortgage-backed securities plunged over a half-point immediately following Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan's Humphrey-Hawkins testimony on Wednesday morning.
By late afternoon, pass-throughs continued to slip to session lows, but yield spreads to Treasuries narrowed by about five to seven basis points, mortgage experts said.
"(Yield) spreads have tightened quite a bit," said one trader at a New York investment house.
"I don't know that there is a lot more upside to spreads now, but most people have been saying that for three weeks," he said.
At 1545 EST/2045 GMT mortgages were 9/32 to 27/32 lower overall. Yield spreads tightened as comparable Treasuries traded off 23/32 to 1-02/32.

In key coupons, Ginnie Mae 30-year 7.5 percent paper was 24/32 lower at 99-26/32, yielding 103 basis points over the 10-year Treasury note. Comparable Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac issues were off 25/32, at 99-20/32 and 99-27/32, respectively. The 10-year note was down 1-02/32 to yield 6.54 percent.
Market sources said the Treasury market was pricing in a 25-basis-point rate hike because of Greenspan's more hawkish-than-anticipated testimony to the Senate Banking Committee.
"It's been a relatively quiet day (in mortgages). Most people have been focusing on the Treasury market," one trader said.
